notes:
I read files directly. I could not run git or cargo in this review, so the diff against the base was inferred from the content and the changed-files list. Items checked:
- Worktree HEAD is the ref refs/heads/sprint/r-4-adrs-and-manifests. I could not resolve the commit hash itself to confirm 59ec838.
- The ADR-SAG-0023 Status line is Active with the (Active, r-4) bullets. The r-3b subsection is Proposed.
- The root Cargo.toml has caret ranges for serde, serde_json, sha2, thiserror, uuid, tempfile and clap 4, mimalloc 0.1.52 and the toml and ureq entries. Exact pins are only sc-observability and sc-observability-types.
- The root Cargo.toml still carries sc-observability-types = "=1.5.0" (line 39). That is intended for r-1 to delete: the sprint doc and plan.md lines 124-128 say so. Until r-1 merges, check-exact-pins.sh fails on that line because the crate is not on the list. So r-4 must merge after r-1 and rebase first.
- The sc-observability-types ownership record is absent from sc-lint.toml. The mimalloc and clap records are added.
- Both crates have default cli, cli = [dep:mimalloc, dep:clap], optional mimalloc and clap, [[bin]] required-features = [cli] and [[test]] cli required-features = [cli]. The main.rs files still have the unconditional #[global_allocator]. The bin is gated, so that compiles.
- tests/cli.rs is the only target using CARGO_BIN_EXE in each crate, and both are gated.
- CI has the lib --no-default-features builds for both crates, the cargo-tree-gates and check-exact-pins steps, and the hack steps for sc-treesitter and sc-agent-types. cargo-tree-gates.sh has the two mimalloc rows in lib mode.
- No std::sync::Mutex or .await code changed, so RULE-ADR-AWAIT-MUTEX does not apply.
- Out of arch-qa scope, for req-qa: the ADR-SAG-0017 amendment says the upstream sc-publish issue URL is 'not yet filed', while the acceptance row asks for the bead and URL to be recorded. Also, boundary manifests for clap and mimalloc are deferred to r-3b and r-3c, as the sprint doc states, and the PR must state the deferral.
